variants.label: two rooms, constant preloaded off the critical path
variants.architecture: Room A runs `@rM*+sH` and ships n^2+n. Room B runs `@1Mr}sH`: it loads B=1 and then blocks on `r`, so the three ops that set up the halving (M 1 W) cost nothing on the critical path -- the wait is free. 9x9, both compute rooms 3x9, I and O in the middle band.

notSubmitted.design: 8x8 single room, hand-built by Alexey, pipes as first drawn
notSubmitted.why: 3-cell input pipe delayed `r` by a tick; 4-cell output pipe cost three more in transit

notSubmitted.design: same 8x8 with both pipes shortened to 2 cells
notSubmitted.why: Kept for the record, deliberately NOT submitted: 960 beats the old 1053 but loses to triangle_02's 891. In 8x8 the compute room cannot exceed a 3x5 interior, and 9 instructions need 4 turns there, so `s` lands on step 14 and 15 ticks is the floor. The footprint win (64 vs 81, 1.27x) does not pay for the tick loss (15 vs 11, 1.36x).
notSubmitted.watchOut: the first line starts with two spaces; strip them and the rooms shift and the program stops parsing (bad pipe glyph at (1,2))

provenBounds: The arithmetic needs 7 compute ops (9 instructions with r and s): BFS over all of M W + - * N % / & | ~ { } and digits finds nothing at depth 6 and exactly two sequences at depth 7 (`M * + M 1 W }`, `M * + M 2 W /`).
In an 8x8 box the largest compute room connectable to I and O is a 3x5 interior (exhaustive search over room placements and legal pipe paths).

Reaching the leaders' 832 needs 13 ticks, i.e. `s` on step 12, i.e. a 12-cell 3-segment walk, i.e. a 3x6 interior -- which does not fit in 8x8 in any layout this search found. Alexey's adjacent I/O rooms showed the model of legal layouts was incomplete once already, so this bound is 'not found', not 'impossible'.
